subject: POC kickoff: AWS Marketplace multi-product listing + invoice reconciliation
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <procurement@acme-analytics.com>, Janelle Park <janelle.park@aws-partner.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: POC kickoff: AWS Marketplace multi-product listing + invoice reconciliation

Hi Carlos / Janelle —

Thanks for agreeing to run the POC for the multi-SKU listing and billing synchronization. Goal is to validate:
- entitlement mapping between AWS Marketplace SKUs and Acme product SKUs
- monthly invoice reconciliation process (consolidated invoice vs per-SKU settlement files)
- any contract redlines needed for SaaS contract + marketplace terms

Attached is our integration checklist to help scope the work (redwood_aws_integration_checklist.xlsx). High-level asks from our side:
1) sample invoice you require for PO/payment approval (attached if you can share)
2) list of Acme SKUs and the desired billing granularity (monthly flat vs usage-metered)
3) point of contact for finance to validate settlement windows (e.g., NET30/NET45)

Proposed pilot window: Nov 29 — Dec 31 (30 days). If that works, we can schedule a 30-min kickoff next week to align owners.

Next steps: Carlos, can you confirm the procurement contact and whether Acme needs consolidated invoice or itemized by SKU? Janelle, can you confirm any AWS-side entitlements/contracting prerequisites we should surface?

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood_aws_integration_checklist.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Carlos Ruiz <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 18:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: AWS Marketplace multi-product listing + invoice reconciliation

Thanks Priya — quick technical notes from the SE side:

- Entitlement model: recommend one entitlement per "product family" with SKU-level usage metrics attached (rather than creating unique entitlement IDs per micro-feature). This simplifies AWS metering calls and downstream reconciliation.
- Metering: we can send per-customer usage records via the AWS Marketplace Metering APIs; those are reconciled on the AWS side and reported in the monthly settlement CSVs. We should confirm whether Acme expects us to transform those CSVs into your invoice schema or if you want raw settlement exports.
- Mapping: I added a first-pass mapping template to the S3 path in the related links (s3://redwood-integration/artifacts/acme/poc-mapping.csv). Please populate column B with Acme SKU ids and column C with desired invoice lines.

Questions for Acme:
- Do you require tax line items on the invoice, or will tax be handled separately?
- Preferred GL code mapping? If you can share one example invoice (PDF) we'll mirror the layout.

I'll be available for a technical kickoff Fri Nov 20 10:00-11:00 PT — ping if that slot works.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Carlos Ruiz <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Morales <lina.morales@acme-analytics.com>, Janelle Park <janelle.park@aws-partner.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: AWS Marketplace multi-product listing + invoice reconciliation

Hi Priya / team —

Thanks for the checklist. A few items from procurement/finance perspective:

- Acme prefers a consolidated monthly invoice referencing our PO (PO# ACME-PO-7581). We can accept per-SKU detail lines within that consolidated invoice.
- Settlement timing: our standard is NET30 from invoice date. Can you confirm Redwood's processing timelines once AWS issues settlement reports? Typical expectation is Redwood issues invoice within 7 business days of receiving AWS settlement CSVs.
- Attached is a sample invoice layout we need (acme_sample_invoice_oct2026.pdf). Please mirror columns: account name, SKU, quantity, unit price, extended amount, tax, total.

Also copying our CFO Lina Morales for any commercial questions. Lina: do you have any preferences around passthrough of AWS fees vs Redwood consolidated billing?

Carlos Ruiz
Procurement Manager, Acme Analytics
Attachments: acme_sample_invoice_oct2026.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <procurement@acme-analytics.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 01:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: AWS Marketplace multi-product listing + invoice reconciliation

Hi Carlos / Priya —

I reviewed the marketplace terms and drafted a couple of redlines to the SaaS addendum we typically push for AWS listings. Main items:
- Clarify indemnity carveouts for marketplace metering discrepancies (we propose mutual reconciliation process with a 60-day window to raise disputes).
- Specify settlement timing: Redwood to invoice within 7 business days of AWS settlement report; payment NET30 thereafter.
- Data handling: add a short clause about settlement CSVs being used only for billing reconciliation (no additional PII retention beyond 90 days).

I uploaded the marked-up doc (legal_redlines_aws_marketplace.docx) and started a DocuSign envelope for the SaaS addendum (link in related_links). If Acme needs different language on passthrough of AWS fees we can handle that in the commercial appendix.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <procurement@acme-analytics.com>, Janelle Park <janelle.park@aws-partner.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: AWS Marketplace multi-product listing + invoice reconciliation

Appreciate the quick responses — proposed mutual action plan (short):
1) Nov 22: technical kickoff (Marissa to lead) + CSV mapping ownership (Acme to populate the S3 mapping file)
2) Nov 24: Redwood to ingest mapping + small sandbox metering run against one customer account
3) Nov 29: pilot start (metering enabled in AWS Marketplace, Redwood issues internal test invoice)
4) Dec 31: pilot close and reconciliation; both parties surface any disputes by Jan 30 (60-day dispute window)

Owners: Acme procurement (Carlos) — mapping + sample invoice; Redwood SE (Marissa) — mapping ingestion + sandbox run; Legal (Laura) — finalize SaaS addendum in DocuSign; Sales (Ben/Priya) — overall coordination.

Deal ID: RDW-ACME-2026-11 — I'll log milestones in HubSpot and share the record (link above). Carlos, can you confirm the Nov 29 pilot-start date and whether NET30 is acceptable?

Thanks,
Priya

From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@aws-partner.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Carlos Ruiz <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC kickoff: AWS Marketplace multi-product listing + invoice reconciliation

Thanks — AWS side is aligned on the proposed plan. A few notes:
- For co-sell enablement we'll need the entitlement mapping (CSV) and the AWS seller ID; please ensure the mapping includes the AWS SKU and the Redwood product ID.
- AWS settlement CSVs are generated monthly; typical lag is ~5 business days after month close depending on region. Redwood should expect that cadence; good to include the 7-business-day invoicing window Laura proposed.
- I'll enable the account for co-sell tracking after I see the populated mapping file and the signed SaaS addendum.

I'll also introduce a marketplace enablement engineer to the kickoff thread separately if needed. Looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Janelle Park
AWS Partner Manager
AWS Marketplace

Attachments: none
